description.description: Closed the bookkeeping gap Sprint 129.43 left open by backfilling manifest.json/pipeline-jobs.json/pipeline-history.json/project.json for the Fatih project entirely through existing public APIs (PipelineJobManager.prepareJobRetry/startStage/persistStageSuccess), re-saving already-existing on-disk stage data as the persisted result, with no AI/FFmpeg provider call and no content change (verified by empty git diff).

Test-only change: updated smoke-production-visual-asset-wiring.ts to pass an explicit RuntimeStorageContext into PipelineStageExecutor.execute and durable claim/lease helpers instead of relying on ambient/implicit runtime storage resolution; tightened an assertion to the more specific VISUAL_ASSET_GENERATION_FAILED reason code.

Executed the real audio and assembly stages for the live 'Fatih Sultan Mehmet'in İstanbul'un Fethine Hazırlanışı' project — the step Sprint 129.41 had explicitly left blocked pending separate authorization before touching the real production project.

Test-only realignment: threaded the explicit RuntimeStorageContext that Sprint 129.41 added to ProjectManager and PipelineStageExecutor.execute call signatures through smoke-animation-motion-plan-contract.ts and smoke-production-scene-video-rendering.ts instead of relying on implicit context; widened one assertion to also accept ANIMATION_RESPONSE_SCHEMA_INVALID alongside WORKER_EXECUTION_FAILED.

Restricted public completed-stage regeneration to fromStage=video, requiring a single canonical completed job for source/preserved stages, unifying runtime-context binding across planning/validation/preparation/mutation-locking, making video/assembly supersession intent mandatory and prevalidated, hardening already-prepared replay, and upgrading the forbidden-production guard to physical realpath/device/inode containment.

Replaced the scene-video provider's single authoritative cover/crop/zoompan chain with a two-layer filter graph (blurred motion background plus centered contained foreground) so square, landscape, and portrait source compositions remain fully visible without distortion, while native 16:9 sources still fill the canvas.

Added an optional canonical stopAfterStage resume boundary from the authenticated production command through the orchestrator and runner to the scheduler; a bounded stage still uses normal resume admission identity and full durable lifecycle but creates no downstream reservation/claim/attempt/dispatch.

Replaced project-directory consumed-receipt scanning in failed terminal settlement with exact current-lineage retry-budget binding validation across reservation, record, lease, claim, and attempt; added write-free replay for an existing valid matching settled receipt and deterministic first-write identity based on terminal attempt finalizedAt when settled is absent.

Wikimedia rate-limits and never-retry-on-429 policy adopted after live testing showed repeated 429s from upload.wikimedia.org when scenes fired back-to-back; a corrected, reachable-contact User-Agent was identified as a likely contributor to harsher rate limiting.

Each additional source (Openverse, Library of Congress/Archive.org, NASA Image and Video Library, Pexels/Pixabay/Unsplash) is scoped as an independent sprint on top of the ADR-019 source-router so none require changing ImageProviderName or VisualAssetPipeline's validation branches again; real stock video sourcing is called out as a separate architectural decision since Visuals only ever produces stills today.

A single "real" ImageProviderName with an internal, extensible source router (Wikimedia Commons first) was chosen instead of one provider name per source, so future real photo sources extend the router without touching ImageProviderName or VisualAssetPipeline's validation branches.

No API key, license allowlist, MIME allowlist, and resolution ranking follow the same fetch/timeout/byte-cap conventions as every other real provider, keeping a single provider-hardening pattern across the codebase.

Public regeneration authority was deliberately restricted to fromStage=video only, with arbitrary-stage regeneration left as explicit future work, to keep the initial completed-stage regeneration surface small and provably safe.

Cover/crop rendering was replaced with a centered, aspect-preserving contained foreground (with cover/crop/zoompan motion kept only in a separate blurred decorative background) so the full source composition stays visible instead of being cropped out.

Project-wide consumed-receipt selection from failed terminal settlement was removed and bound instead to the current attempt's exact reservation/record/lease/claim/attempt authority, closing a cross-stage replay hole where a receipt for one stage could be mistakenly reused for another.

A bounded, per-stage OPENAI_ASSEMBLY_MAX_TOKENS (default 3200, inclusive 1600-6000) was added, mirroring the earlier per-stage token-budget pattern, so assembly's AI planning call fails closed on truncation instead of silently producing malformed output.

Ordinal-5 retry attempts are unconditionally rejected and a retry-budget extension requires a single-use, cryptographically bound authority record (not a config flag), so extending the budget for one failed attempt can never be silently reused for a later unrelated failure.
Canonical shared-path check-then-delete cleanup was removed in favor of an operation-owned quarantine primitive, closing a time-of-check-to-time-of-use race in lock/gate/stale cleanup.

A canonical failed-settlement callback completes lease release, claim abandon, record cancellation, and recovery/quiescence validation in one sequence so a failed attempt's durable authorities never linger half-released.

V3 backup manifests use a canonical source runtime authority and unchanging runtime-tree-sha256-v1 aggregate contract; V1/V2 legacy formats are retained read-only for portability but same-authority restore from them fails closed, so authority binding can never be silently downgraded.

Canonical identity is built only from completed durable readback (never from pre-plan/request/fallback authority) and completed-preparation tokens are frozen and WeakMap-owned, so a forged or cloned token can never acquire capability.

Two-phase publication with a PortableNoClobberFilePublisher and typed AudioCanonicalAdmissionConflictError separates security rejection from normal failure, so a foreign-file conflict is preserved rather than treated as an ordinary retryable error.

A mutation-free audit catalogued 28 production storage entrypoint families (11 READY, 7 REQUIRES ADAPTER, 1 REQUIRES MIGRATION, 5 REQUIRES POLICY DECISION, 4 BLOCKING) before any relocation/cutover work, so runtime root relocation cannot begin without first proving every entrypoint's blast radius.
Candidate bytes are sourced only from a verified backup payload, never a live runtime copy, so a migration candidate can never silently diverge from the last verified backup.

Centralized RuntimeProtectedRoots/RuntimePathPolicy/GuardedRuntimeFilesystem primitives give every later runtime-mutating sprint (backup, migration, relocation) a single reparse-aware, containment-checked write path instead of each reimplementing safe writes.

ATOLYE_RUNTIME_ROOT was introduced as a configurable storage root (defaulting to the legacy process.cwd()/data/projects) specifically so a later zero-tracked-runtime policy (Sprint 129.25C) could be introduced without an immediate breaking migration.

The animation provider contract was narrowed to only motionType/start/end/transition, with platform-owned fields (sceneId, sourceImageAssetId, durationSeconds, createdAt) derived from trusted context after validation instead of echoed by the AI provider, closing a class of strict-schema-vs-echo mismatch failures.

AnimationAssetPipeline was converting known provider/scene/phase errors into a generic code, losing the real failure reason; AnimationMotionPlanError now carries safe, specific evidence (sceneId, phase, provider/model, HTTP status, finish reason) instead.

VisualManager was not propagating the observed AI_RESPONSE_TRUNCATED error code before parsing, so a truncated response was misclassified as AI_RESPONSE_INVALID_JSON; a bounded OPENAI_VISUALS_MAX_TOKENS (2000-6000) was added alongside the fix.

createdAt was moved from provider-supplied to application-owned across research/script/visuals so a provider emitting an unexpected timestamp field could no longer fail strict schema validation after an otherwise-complete, non-truncated response.

A centralized, rule-based job transition model (queued->running/cancelled, running->completed/failed/cancelled, failed/cancelled->queued retry, completed terminal) replaced ad hoc status writes, closing races between cancellation and in-flight persistence.

getNextPipelineStage() only fires downstream job creation after a running->completed transition, and completed source plus the missing downstream queued job are persisted in the same atomic write, keeping the deterministic one-job-per-project-per-stage model idempotent under retries and concurrent completion.

A frozen schema v1 persistence adapter (transaction, operation journal, idempotency, reservation) was built and left disabled/preview-only, deliberately deferring dispatch/execution/provider/worker/UI wiring to later sprints.

The content-addressed lookup index is explicitly a derived artifact rebuilt deterministically from canonical records, never an authorization or business-decision source, so a missing or corrupt index can never itself grant or deny execution.
The handler is called exactly once and only a safe serializable summary is persisted to the journal, so raw error stacks, secrets, or uncontrolled payloads can never leak into durable records.
PipelineRunner.runStage was wrapped with an optional durable adapter so legacy behavior is preserved when the adapter is absent, letting the durable layer be integrated without a second orchestrator.
ATOLYE_DURABLE_PIPELINE_EXECUTION=enabled gates the durable adapter so legacy behavior is preserved by default while all pipeline run/retry/resume entrypoints share one composition factory.
This sprint closed the Sprint 99-108 Durable Production Execution phase; bootstrapRecovery classifies durable attempts write-free and never itself reschedules terminal attempts.

A created->starting->ready->draining->stopped/failed state model ensures a worker cannot become ready until recovery initialization and verification are fully successful, avoiding a partially-initialized worker accepting work.

Animation stage was redefined to produce a scene-level motion-plan artifact (schemaVersion 2, artifactType motion-plan, no filePath/url) rather than physical media, keeping physical rendering concentrated in the Video stage instead of duplicating a media-rendering path.

Stream-copy is only attempted when scene/narration duration differs by at most 1/30s and codec/profile/timebase match exactly; otherwise the scene is clone-pad/trim re-encoded, keeping fast-path assembly from silently producing drifted output.
continueProject() is bounded and non-recursive, running at most one stage per call, specifically to close a race where concurrent dispatchers could jump past the assembly boundary into thumbnail.

Provider explicit failure never produces false-success, and on an indeterminate timeout/upload the publishing intent is preserved rather than automatically retried, to avoid a duplicate remote video upload.

An atomic youtube-publish-recovery.json receipt is written before the canonical publish result, so a crash after a successful remote upload but before canonical persistence can be promoted to canonical on restart without a second upload.

reconcilePublish only ever promotes a `matched` result to canonical published state and never itself starts an upload, using priority order canonical published -> recovery receipt -> publishing intent reconciliation.

The full canonical stage order (Research through Export) was run end-to-end via the real PipelineRunner.run() entrypoint on a deterministic fixture rather than a second validation harness, so the same production wiring is exercised rather than a parallel one.

ProductionReadinessService defines READY/NOT_CONFIGURED/INVALID/UNAVAILABLE/BLOCKED so overall ready=true can only be produced when every critical check is READY; readiness itself never makes a paid provider call or mutates user projects.

OpenAIAnimationProvider validates the motion-plan JSON against an exact-key schema with prototype-pollution and depth limits and never determines scene/source identity or file locators itself, keeping identity/locator authority in AnimationStorage.

The execute CLI now requires an explicit --topic and removed the built-in production topic fallback, and slug is deterministic from topic+runId, so a resume can never silently pick up a different topic than the original run.

The first paid production execute produced a successful, non-fallback OpenAI call that still failed strict artifact validation; createdAt was removed from the research provider schema and application-owned canonically instead, and OPENAI_RESEARCH_MAX_TOKENS (default 3200, 1600-6000) was added.

Resume no longer sends a failed start stage directly to the scheduler; a shared prepareFailedStageRetry primitive performs durable reconciliation and CAS-controlled job preparation first, closing a path where a failed job required manual retry and the CLI closed with PRODUCTION_ACCEPTANCE_EXECUTION_FAILED without starting any stage.

Recurring pattern across the 129.x remediation sprints: passing regression suites and independent review does not itself authorize spending real provider credits or mutating the real production project - a separate, explicit operator authorization step is always required before real production execution, consistent with the codebase's fail-closed design.

AI-generated painterly illustration (muted brown/grey tones, dramatic overcast sky) showing a foreground wooden warehouse stocked with sacks, barrels and crates, opening onto a shoreline where armored soldiers with helmets and spears haul a massive iron chain across the beach toward a large three-masted sailing ship flying a red flag with a white crescent moon; fortified towers are visible in the misty background. Composition reads as a military logistics/preparation scene for a siege, consistent with the project's theme of Mehmed the Conqueror's preparations before the siege of Constantinople.

AI-generated photorealistic 2x2 grid image showing Ottoman soldiers in red robes and distinctive white börk hats with red bands (Janissary-style dress): one drawing a bow before fellow archers at a castle gate, one wielding a curved sword near cannon barrels, blacksmiths forging weapons/cannon parts at a glowing forge, and a soldier carrying a breastplate near wooden siege equipment and army tents. Cinematic, dramatic lighting, stone fortress backdrop consistent with a siege-preparation scene for the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople.

AI-generated painterly image depicting a young Ottoman sultan in royal red robe, fur-trimmed mantle, white turban, and sword, standing in a dim ornate palace hall beside an empty throne. He gazes at a large map propped on an easel showing a peninsula between two waterways (resembling the Bosphorus/Golden Horn around Constantinople) with a red X marking a target location. Composition and lighting (chiaroscuro, oil-painting style) evoke a moment of strategic planning before a siege, directly illustrating the project's theme of Mehmed the Conqueror preparing for the conquest of Istanbul.

AI-generated cinematic painterly image depicting a group of bearded Ottoman officials/advisors wearing red fez-style headwear (kavuk), seated around a dark wooden table in an ornate candlelit chamber. A large map is spread across the table alongside books, bound documents, and a lit candle in a brass holder; a crystal chandelier hangs overhead and a curtained window is visible in the background. The composition (map + advisors in deliberation) strongly evokes a war council/strategy session, consistent with the project's theme of Mehmed II's preparations for the Conquest of Istanbul (1453).

AI-generated painterly illustration depicting a nighttime bronze cannon foundry scene: massive Ottoman siege cannons being cast with glowing molten metal poured from a large crucible, sparks and dark smoke filling the sky. In the foreground a bearded man in a turban and dark robe studies architectural blueprints showing wooden siege-tower/scaffold structures, pencil in hand. In the background, tall wooden siege towers or construction scaffolding stand before crenellated fortress walls, with groups of soldiers/workers gathered near them. The dramatic chiaroscuro lighting, muted browns/oranges against dark smoke, and historical Ottoman dress evoke the technical/military preparations (cannon-casting and siege engineering) undertaken before the 1453 siege of Constantinople.

AI-generated cinematic digital painting depicting a vast column of armored Ottoman infantry (spearmen/pikemen in helmets and mail, carrying round shields) marching in fog toward a massive crenellated stone fortress wall with multiple towers. Large siege cannons and a military camp of canvas tents are visible in the foreground/midground. Red flags bearing the white Ottoman crescent-and-star emblem are raised throughout the ranks. Dark, moody, overcast sky lends a dramatic, foreboding atmosphere. This visual clearly illustrates the Ottoman army's siege preparations and march against the fortified walls of Constantinople, matching the project's theme of Mehmed the Conqueror's preparation for the conquest of Istanbul.
